t: r/homelab on Reddit: Re-enabling NIC Teaming (LBFO) in Windows 10 & other desktop SKUs, even after Microsoft removed it
s: September 19, 2019 - Normally Windows would scale the number of connections based on factors such as the number of available channels, advertised RSS queue counts, and the number of adapters in each LAG, but that last part of the scaling doesn't work because Intel's implementation is proprietary and Windows doesn't know anything about the LAG. The only way to solve this is to use native NIC teaming (LBFO), but Windows 10 doesn't have support for it even in the Pro Workstation SKU - it's restricted to server SKUs only.

t: GitHub - hifihedgehog/Windows11LBFO: Adds LBFO NIC teaming support to your Windows 11 system with a single script run.
s: This repository provides scripts to enable Load Balancing/Failover (LBFO) and NIC teaming on Windows 11 installations, which is not natively supported. The Install-LBFO.ps1 script installs the LBFO provider, Uninstall-LBFO.ps1 removes it, and Verify-LBFO-Cleanup.ps1 checks for residual LBFO configurations.
